chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A woman left behind her husband, her brothers from her mother, and her sisters from her father. He said: For the husband is the half, which is three shares; and for the brothers from the mother is the third, the male and the female are equal in it; and a share remains, so it is for the brothers and sisters from the father, for the male is like the share of the two females, because the shares do not increase (due to deficiency) and the husband is not reduced from the half, nor the brothers from the mother from their third.
So if they are more than that, they are partners in the third.

And if there is one, then for her is the sixth. And what Allah Blessed and High meant by His words: 'And if a man is inherited by a Kalala or a woman, and for him is a brother or a sister, so for each one of them is the sixth. So if they are more than that, they are partners in the third' — He meant by that specifically the brothers and sisters from the mother.

They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the Kalala. If a person dies and has no child, and for him is a sister, meaning a sister from mother and father or a sister from father, so for her is half of what he left, and he inherits her if there is no child for her.

And if they are brothers, men and women, then for the male is like the share of the two females. So they are the ones who are increased and decreased, and similarly are their children who are increased and decreased.

And if a woman left her husband, her brothers from her mother, and her two sisters from her father, then for the husband is the half, three shares, and for the brothers from the mother are two shares, and a share remains, so it is for the two sisters from the father. And if there was one, it is for her, because the two sisters from the father, if they were two brothers from the father, would not be increased over what remains. And if there was one, or there was in the place of the one a brother, he would not be increased over what remains. And the female from the sisters and from the children is not increased over what if it were a male, it would not be increased upon him.

key_terms.الْإِخْوَةُ مِنَ الْأُمِّ: Brothers and sisters from the mother (maternal siblings)
key_terms.الْكَلالَةُ: Kalala (one who has no direct ascendants or descendants)
key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: For the male is the share of two females

ai.seo_question: How are inheritance shares distributed when a deceased leaves a husband, maternal siblings, and paternal siblings?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the specific mechanics of inheritance distribution involving mixed siblings (maternal and paternal) alongside a spouse, resolving potential conflicts in share allocation. It provides a detailed exegesis of the term 'Kalala' in Surah An-Nisa, clarifying that the verse regarding siblings inheriting one-sixth specifically applies to maternal siblings in this context, while paternal siblings take the residual share. The narration underscores the principle that shares are not reduced below their Quranic minimums, even when the total exceeds the estate's base units.
